findings.title: A global group view grant authorizes group creation
findings.body: `canManage()` accepts either the `view` or `manage` scope. `GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup()` uses this no-argument check before creating a group, so an administrator granted only the Groups `view` scope can create top-level groups. The view scope must not be considered sufficient for `canManage()`; only `manage` should authorize this write operation.

findings.title: Group member filtering returns authorization resource IDs instead of group IDs
findings.body: The callback passes `groupResource.getId()` into `hasPermission()` and later returns that value in `granted`, but schema-created individual resources are named with the `GroupModel` ID while their authorization-resource ID is a distinct generated ID. The lookup therefore misses the individual resource and falls back to the all-groups resource; when that fallback does grant access, the returned IDs still cannot match user group memberships. `UsersResource` and the brute-force endpoint use this set for provider-side group filtering and user counts, so scoped `view-members`/`manage-members` grants produce empty or incomplete counts and paginated searches. Evaluate the resource being iterated and return the corresponding actual group ID (while handling the aggregate Groups resource separately).

findings.title: Per-object schema resources are never assigned their resource type
findings.body: `getOrCreateResource()` creates an individual resource and assigns scopes but never calls `resource.setType(resourceType)`. `GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` discovers individual group resources exclusively through `resourceStore.findByType(..., "Groups", ...)`, so resources created for single-group policies are not enumerated at all. As a result, member-based user filtering cannot obtain the groups authorized by those policies. Set the resource type when creating the resource and migrate any already-created per-object resources as needed.

findings.title: Existing admin-permissions clients are not upgraded with the Groups schema
findings.body: `init()` returns immediately when an admin-permissions client already exists. A realm that enabled V2 before this change therefore retains only the old Users/Clients scopes and aggregate resources; it never receives the new group scopes or the aggregate `Groups` resource. Creating a group scope permission in such a realm reaches `getOrCreateResource()` and fails because the requested scopes do not exist, making the newly added authorization type unusable after upgrade. Initialization must be idempotent and add missing schema scopes/resources for existing clients, or a migration must backfill them.
